nodes.name: Lead webhook
nodes.notes: rawBody is ON so the HMAC is checked against the exact bytes the site sent. Re-serialising parsed JSON would not reliably reproduce them.

nodes.name: Process lead
nodes.notes: Calls the process_lead RPC: upserts the contact and creates a follow-up task in one transaction. Idempotent — a webhook retry will not duplicate either.

nodes.name: Notify LINE (optional)
nodes.notes: Disabled by default. Enable once LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN and LINE_ADMIN_USER_ID are set on your n8n instance. The site already sends the client confirmation and the admin email via Resend, so this is an extra channel, not a replacement.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, leadId: $json.leadId, contactId: $json.contactId, taskId: $json.taskId, taskCreated: $json.taskCreated }) }}

nodes.name: Respond 401
nodes.notes: An unsigned or wrongly signed request is rejected outright. The webhook URL on its own is not a credential.

nodes.name: Respond 422
nodes.notes: The signature was good but the lead could not be processed — most often an id that is not in the database yet.

nodes.name: Notify Telegram
nodes.notes: Disabled by default: the site sends this alert itself, from src/lib/crm.ts, so a lead reaches you with no automation host running. Telegram has no idempotency — leaving this enabled alongside the in-process alert sends every lead twice. Enable it here only if you also drop notifyTelegram from src/app/api/leads/route.ts.
